page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.2xlarge is a burstable virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, fall into the bottom 25% tier, with single-threaded compression and decompression tasks showing weak to poor throughput. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as multi-threaded Geekbench, PassMark CPU, and stress-ng multi-core tests, achieve average performance. Memory bandwidth and Redis SET operations also register in the middle 50% tier, demonstrating stable throughput under multi-threaded execution.

Operating on a burstable CPU allocation model, this instance offers a cost-effective profile for workloads with variable CPU utilization. The primary tradeoff is the reliance on CPU credits to sustain peak performance, alongside a 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth which limits continuous high-throughput networking. Consequently, the ecs.t6-c1m4.2xlarge is best suited for general-purpose workloads with intermittent resource demands, such as development environments, low-traffic web serving, code compilation, and lightweight database operations.
